$comment: Per-machine installer facts for Pitwall (family ADR 0053 section 2.1 and 3). stopExclusions: programs of the bundle that stop-all must not end (none: the installer removes the service's registration first, then ends the server and the app in every session). survivesForcedEnd: the adoption's statement that every program in the stop list survives a forced end without losing more than its last unfinished write; each entry names what was checked.

survivesForcedEnd.why: The app window keeps its own state in app-state.json, written to a .new file and renamed (app/src-tauri/src/app_state.rs, AppState::save); a forced end leaves the old file whole. Its jobs (model load, benchmark, service install) are requests to the server or the service verbs, which finish or fail on their own.

Every file the server owns (settings, presets, usage, metrics, benchmarks, engine pins, the app records, the admin key, the discovery file) is written through paths::write_atomic, a temporary file and a rename that keeps a backup (crates/pitwall-server/src/paths.rs); the response cache is SQLite in WAL mode with synchronous NORMAL (crates/pitwall-server/src/cache_db.rs), which loses at most the last unflushed transactions and stays consistent. A model download writes a .part file that is verified and then renamed (crates/pitwall-server/src/library.rs), so a forced end leaves a partial file that is never loaded, and the next download starts again. A running model process belongs to the server and ends with it.
